clue.text: Grub Street journalist's worn-out horse

definitions.meaning: a writer of mediocre work for hire, the trade associated with Grub Street
an old or tired horse hired out for riding

explanation.surface: A down-at-heel London scribbler owns a tired old nag.
explanation.walkthrough: Grub Street was an old London street of struggling hired writers, now a byword for literary hackwork.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses come from 'hackney', a horse for hire, later extended to a writer who works for pay.

clue.text: Dance requiring two wind instruments

parts.note: a horn is a wind instrument, the first of the pair
a pipe is the second wind instrument

explanation.surface: A dance that needs two woodwind or brass players.
explanation.definitionFit: The hornpipe is a lively solo dance traditionally associated with sailors.

clue.text: Class teacher initially involved in court action

indicators.note: involved in means wrapped up within, so the letter goes inside the lawsuit

parts.note: a case is a lawsuit or action in court

indicators.note: initially asks for only the first letter of teacher

explanation.surface: A schoolteacher gets caught up in a lawsuit over a lesson.
explanation.definitionFit: A caste is a hereditary social class, especially in Hindu society.

clue.text: Very clean place where the French sought at first

parts.note: a spot is a place or location
les is the French plural word for 'the'

indicators.note: at first asks for only the opening letter of the word sought

explanation.surface: A spotless location where French people went looking for something.
explanation.definitionFit: Spotless means without a single mark or stain, so thoroughly clean.

clue.text: Rapid growth of port airline being developed

indicators.note: being developed suggests the letters of of port airline are being worked into a new form

explanation.surface: An airline at a port is expanding fast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' looks like a link word but is part of the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Proliferation is fast multiplication or spread, a rapid increase in number.

clue.text: Be inclined to accept start of recent craze

indicators.note: to accept means to take in, so the first word holds the letter

parts.note: to tend is to be inclined

indicators.note: start of asks for the first letter of recent

explanation.surface: Being prone to go along with the latest fad.
explanation.definitionFit: A trend is a passing fashion or general movement, much like a craze.

clue.text: Teach Europeans about old Continental coin

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the pair of letters goes round the coin

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for European, so EE is two of them
the ducat was a gold or silver coin once used across Europe

explanation.surface: Teaching Europeans about an old currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reads as 'on the subject of' but signals one piece placed around another.
explanation.definitionFit: To educate is to instruct or train, which is teaching.

clue.text: In the Kent area it's where builders may be working

indicators.note: In placed first means the following word goes inside the region

parts.note: SE stands for the South East of England, where Kent lies

explanation.surface: A building plot in Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in South East England, so SE.
explanation.definitionFit: A building site is the plot where construction takes place.

clue.text: Certify where cricket enthusiasts may be?

definitions.meaning: cricket fans may be at a Test, a full international match

explanation.surface: Confirming the venue where fans of cricket gather.
explanation.walkthrough: A Test is an international cricket match, so fans may be AT TEST.
explanation.definitionFit: Attest means to bear witness or certify formally; the second sense is a whimsical split.

clue.text: Rice dish originally taken by drunkard in Brazilian port

indicators.note: in places the drunkard and his letter within the name of the port

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is Brazil's great port city
a sot is a habitual drunk

indicators.note: originally asks for the first letter of taken, which comes just after the drunkard

explanation.surface: A rice dish first sampled by a drinker in Rio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'originally taken by drunkard' gives SOT followed by T; that pair goes 'in' RIO.
explanation.definitionFit: Risotto is an Italian dish of rice cooked slowly in stock.

clue.text: Blow up, being rather uptight? Not entirely

indicators.note: not entirely says we take only part of the words rather uptight, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: Someone tense enough to lose their temper, but only half-way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not entirely' signals the answer sits inside 'rather uptight'.
explanation.definitionFit: To blow up is to explode, as a volcano or a temper does when it erupts.

clue.text: Calm-sounding composition

indicators.note: sounding tells us to take a word that is said like the calm word but spelt differently

parts.note: peace is a state of calm

explanation.surface: A tranquil-sounding musical work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sounding' signals a homophone: PEACE and PIECE are said alike.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece is a single work of music, writing or art.

clue.text: Fashionable girl meeting an inhabitant of Mumbai, perhaps

parts.note: in means fashionable or in vogue
Di is a short girl's name, from Diana

explanation.surface: A trendy young woman meets someone from Mumbai.
explanation.definitionFit: Mumbai is a city in India, so one who lives there is an example of an Indian; 'perhaps' marks the example.

clue.text: Coffee English journalists dipped into thus

indicators.note: dipped into means put inside, so the journalists go within the word for thus

parts.note: so means thus
the press is journalists as a group

explanation.surface: English reporters dunk something in their coffee.
explanation.definitionFit: Espresso is strong black coffee made by forcing steam through ground beans.

clue.text: Futility of free spinet lessons?

indicators.note: free suggests the letters of spinet lessons are let loose and rearranged

explanation.surface: Is it futile to take free lessons on the spinet?
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' reads as 'at no cost' but is the anagram signal; a spinet is a small harpsichord.
explanation.definitionFit: Futility is the quality of being useless or without purpose, which is pointlessness.

clue.text: Breathing device provided by popular, healthy king

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable
hale means healthy, as in hale and hearty
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A medical aid supplied by a well-liked, fit monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: An inhaler delivers medicine for breathing, often used for asthma.

clue.text: Take clothes off before beginning to enter bar

indicators.note: before places the undressing word ahead of the next piece

parts.note: to strip is to undress

indicators.note: beginning to asks for the first letter of enter

explanation.surface: Undressing before going into a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' looks like a pub but means a band or line.
explanation.definitionFit: A stripe is a band of colour, like a bar on a flag or uniform.

clue.text: Female artist engaging quiet Nepali mountain guide

parts.note: she is the female pronoun

indicators.note: engaging means taking on or holding, so the artist holds the quiet letter

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a recognised artist
p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet

explanation.surface: A woman painter hires a hushed Himalayan guide.
explanation.definitionFit: Sherpas are a Himalayan people of Nepal famed as guides and porters on mountain expeditions.

clue.text: Acted as administrator of church farm

parts.note: ran means managed or administered

explanation.surface: Someone who ran a church farm.
explanation.definitionFit: A ranch is a large farm, especially one for raising cattle in the Americas.

clue.text: Haggard equestrian?

definitions.meaning: H. ... Haggard was the novelist who wrote King Solomon's Mines

explanation.surface: A gaunt, worn-looking horseman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Haggard' reads as 'gaunt' but is the surname of the author H. Rider Haggard.
explanation.definitionFit: The novelist's middle name, and the ordinary word for someone on horseback.

clue.text: Garment worn when sweltering in the outskirts of Delhi?

indicators.note: in places the heat word inside those edge letters
the outskirts of asks for only the edge letters of Delhi, the first and last

parts.note: sweltering means very hot

explanation.surface: Clothing worn in the heat around India's capital.
explanation.definitionFit: A dhoti is a loincloth worn by men in India, wrapped around the waist and legs.

clue.text: Part of meadow flower, primarily?

parts.note: a lea is a meadow or grassland

indicators.note: primarily asks for the opening letter of flower

explanation.surface: A piece of a wild flower in a field.
explanation.definitionFit: A leaf is part of a plant, so part of a flower growing in a meadow.

clue.text: Woman's lines, penetrating even for a poet

indicators.note: penetrating means getting inside, so the lines go into the poetic word

parts.note: e'en is the poetic contraction of even
L is short for line, so LL means lines

explanation.surface: A woman's lines in a verse play, even poetic ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Ellen is a woman's first name, so it stands for a woman.

clue.text: Godless little devil with evidence of debts

parts.note: an imp is a small devil or mischievous child
IOUs ('I owe you') are written notes acknowledging debts

explanation.surface: An irreligious young rascal holding a pile of written debts.
explanation.definitionFit: Impious means lacking reverence for God, as a godless person does.

clue.text: Distant object, a coin of low denomination once

definitions.text: a coin of low denomination once

parts.note: far means distant
a thing is an object

explanation.surface: A faraway object turns out to be an old low-value coin.
explanation.walkthrough: The farthing was a British coin worth a quarter of an old penny, withdrawn in 1961.
explanation.definitionFit: The farthing was the smallest British coin in use before decimalisation.

clue.text: One who habitually drinks at home, without going outside

indicators.note: going outside means the abbreviation wraps around the home word

parts.note: W/O is the written abbreviation for without
in means at home

explanation.surface: A solitary drinker who stays home and never ventures out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without going outside' reads as staying in, but 'without' gives WO, which goes outside IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A wino is a heavy drinker, typically of cheap wine.
